signals.title: USD/JPY — G10 Bilateral Theme + Hawkish BoJ Pivot
signals.text: JPY's G10-leading 1W momentum (+2.986%) and the BoJ's hawkish hold at 1.0% drive persistent JPY strength against the weakest G10 peer, the USD (-1.567%). Crowded JPY COT short -114.0k (73% short) fuels an ongoing squeeze as US-JGB real rate differentials narrow despite the +267bp OIS carry advantage. The upcoming US labor market data is the catalyst for determining if the USD/JPY sell-off toward 157.40 extends.

signals.title: GBP/USD — Long Positioning Crowding + Carry Neutrality
signals.text: GBP COT lev_net long +33.8k (66% long) creates profit-taking risk at the 1.3487 resistance as the carry advantage vs USD has vanished to -8bp on an OIS basis. While BoE real rates (+0.93%) remain restrictive, the rally toward 1.35 is vulnerable to a bull-trap if US labor data surprises hawkishly. The next BoE meeting (mkt: 100% hold priced) is the catalyst for resolving the neutral market bias.

signals.title: EUR/USD — COT Short Squeeze + ECB Hike Bias
signals.text: EUR COT lev_net short -80.5k (68% short) faces significant squeeze risk as firm Eurozone inflation supports the ECB's hike bias and narrows the real rate gap. EUR/USD closed at 1.1527, holding above its SMA20 (1.1424) and SMA50 (1.1487), despite a +146bp OIS carry disadvantage favoring the USD. The next ECB meeting (mkt: 51% hike priced) on 10 Sep is the catalyst for validating this hawkish divergence.

signals.title: USD/CAD — Extreme COT Short + Technical Breakdown
signals.text: CAD COT lev_net short -99.8k (81.2% short) sets up a massive contrarian reversal risk as USD/CAD breaks below key trendlines to close at 1.4017. Negative correlation with WTI (z=-1.54σ) has decoupled, leaving the pair sensitive to a squeeze on any US Dollar softening. The next BoC meeting (mkt: 100% hold priced) on 9 Sep is the catalyst for a fundamental shift in the 1.40 handle support.

signals.title: AUD/USD — Negative ESI + Retail Short Bias
signals.text: AUD/USD faces downward pressure from a negative ESI (-14.7) and disappointing data, despite a +70bp OIS carry advantage and a 40% priced RBA hike bias. Retail sentiment is extremely short (70%), which often acts as a contrarian support level near 0.7024, but poor data momentum limits upside. The next RBA meeting (mkt: 24% hike priced) on 11 Aug is the catalyst for confirming the restrictive +0.39% real rate trajectory.
